title: Brownfield Spec-Driven Change Workflow
description: The read-only discovery, approval gates, Spec Kit artifacts, implementation, validation, review, and local squash-merge flow used for this architecture reduction. No remote push is part of the flow.

diagrams.title: Brownfield Spec-Driven Change Workflow
diagrams.description: Start with repository evidence, gate writes on compatibility and approval, then move from spec to plan, tasks, implementation, validation, and a reviewed local merge.
diagrams.accessibility: A left-to-right workflow begins with a read-only repository baseline and pinned-tool compatibility check. Missing Spec Kit setup is initialized only after conflict inspection. Brownfield scan informs approved project templates and a testable spec. Planning, task generation, and analysis precede incremental implementation. Validation and checks loop back to implementation on failure. A full diff review and latest-main integration gate the local squash merge; remote push is excluded.

nodes.label: 1. Read-only baseline: status, dirty paths, guidance
2. Check Spec Kit and Brownfield compatibility
Stop and resolve pin or environment mismatch
Spec Kit scaffold already present?
Initialize Codex skills only after checking conflicts
3. Brownfield scan: code, contracts, docs, quality gates
Project profile or templates need changes?
Wait for explicit bootstrap approval
4. Tailor constitution and templates from verified facts
5. Specify stories, requirements, exclusions, acceptance
Material ambiguity remains?
Resolve scope with the user, then update spec
6. Plan: research, model, contracts, quickstart
7. Generate ordered implementation tasks
8. Analyze spec, plan, and tasks for gaps
9. Implement approved scope in small slices
10. Brownfield validate read-only
Run authorized formatting, build, test, link checks
11. Review full diff and preserve pre-existing work
Integrate latest local main; resolve conflicts
12. Squash merge into local main
No remote push or publish
